name: 482. BytePlus and MiniMax /content stream the file a task names, through the SSRF-checked media fetcher (media fetcher stream)
description: Local fixture regression for TXE-7036, no live provider calls. Start tests/e2e/api/runners/provider-error-fixture.mjs and an isolated gateway on tests/e2e/api/provider_config/provider-error-fixture.config.json, whose byteplus and minimax providers have the fixture as base URL and the fixture's media tunnel as proxy_config, and run with providerErrorFixture=1; every case is skipped otherwise. A finished BytePlus or MiniMax task names its file by URL, and the gateway fetches that URL through the SSRF-hardened media fetcher, which refuses a loopback address. The fixture's task fixture-media-gapped therefore names its file at http://203.0.113.10 (TEST-NET-3: public to the check, routed nowhere), which the gateway reaches only through the provider's proxy: the media tunnel joins the CONNECT to the fixture, which sends a 512 KiB file in two halves 1.5 seconds apart. 482.2 and 482.3 download through GET /v1/videos/{id}/content by way of the fixture's download probe, which reports when the first byte reached it against when the fixture wrote the second half. 482.4 and 482.5 ask for the task fixture-media-loopback, whose file is on the fixture's own loopback address: the gateway must refuse it without asking for the file. 482.6 reads the counters: each task was queried once per download, the gapped file was asked for once per provider with the public address as its Host, a tunnel to that address was opened, and the loopback file was never asked for. Before the change both providers read the file whole before answering (FetchMediaURL), so the first byte of a download could only follow the file host's last. The Go tests cover the 256 MiB cap, redirects, credentials and the other five providers, which no fixture route stands in for.
